evals.name: publication-confirmation
evals.prompt: I have a completed team meeting guide in meeting-guide.md. Publish it as a Confluence page.
evals.expected_output: The agent treats the publication request as confirmed, consumes the destination answers already supplied (space, parent, title, language) without re-asking or inventing others, and shows the complete operation summary before publishing.
expectations: Does not publish before resolving the destination and operation.

Consumes the destination answers supplied in the instructions (space, parent, title, language); only when one is genuinely missing does it ask for it, rather than re-asking for answered details or inventing values.
Summarizes the irreversible operation before executing it.

evals.name: stable-id-preservation
evals.prompt: Create a Confluence page from this Markdown architecture guide (architecture-guide.md in this workspace). Translate the visible prose into Italian, but preserve all stable IDs, status values, API operation names, URLs, and code exactly.
evals.expected_output: The page content is translated only where requested while machine-facing identifiers and document structure remain unchanged.
expectations: Preserves stable IDs and machine-facing status values exactly.
Preserves headings, tables, links, and conditional N/A reasons.
Translates human-facing prose without translating code, URLs, or operation names.
Omits a leading H1 when it exactly matches the Confluence page title, while preserving other headings.

A stable `<!-- id: ... -->` marker kept in the prepared representation may be dropped outright by Confluence on import (HTML comments are not representable on every write route); that platform limitation does not violate the ID rule. Only mangling it into visible or escaped text (`\<!--`, `<!--`) is a failure.

evals.name: safe-update
evals.prompt: Make your own working copy of the seed Design Review page at https://pagopa.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DevEx/pages/3313926515 by copying it under the DevEx Playground folder https://pagopa.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DevEx/folder/3314123072 with a unique title of your choice (e.g. append the current date and time). Never modify the seed page itself. Then update the page copy you created with the contents of design-review.md (in this workspace). Keep the document status unchanged and do not create any additional duplicate page. Return the updated copy's URL.
evals.expected_output: The agent first creates one fresh working copy of the seed page, then resolves and fetches that copy, updates that copy, preserves its status, avoids creating further duplicates, and returns the updated copy's URL.
expectations: Creates exactly one fresh working copy of the seed page and never edits the seed page itself.
Uses the created copy as the update target without making any further duplicate page.
Does not change lifecycle status merely because publication occurred.
Returns the updated page URL only after a successful update.

evals.name: deterministic-markdown-preparation
evals.prompt: Make your own working copy of the seed Design Review page at https://pagopa.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DevEx/pages/3313926515 by copying it under the DevEx Playground folder https://pagopa.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DevEx/folder/3314123072 with a unique title of your choice (e.g. append the current date and time). Never modify the seed page itself. The page copy you create contains an expand macro (a collapsible section). Publish the soft-wrapped design-review.md (design-review-softwrapped.md in this workspace; paragraph lines are broken for readability) to that page copy.
evals.expected_output: The agent first creates one fresh working copy of the seed page, then runs scripts/prepare_markdown.py to collapse the soft-wraps into one logical line per paragraph, applies the leading-H1 rule relative to the copy's title (omitting a leading H1 only when it exactly matches that title and keeping every other heading), keeps the collapsible expand section (and any callout/info blocks) as Confluence macros instead of flattening or deleting them, updates the page copy, and verifies content parity.
expectations: Creates a fresh working copy of the seed page and never edits the seed page itself.
Runs the bundled prepare_markdown.py and uses its output as the body.
Applies the leading-H1 rule relative to the copy's title: omits a leading H1 that exactly matches that title and keeps it (with every other heading) otherwise.

Does NOT delete or flatten Confluence-only rich content (expand/collapsible sections, info/note/tip/warning/error callouts) to make a Markdown push pass; it preserves those nodes as macros or stops and asks the user.
When the incoming source itself declares such constructs (e.g. a <details> block or an admonition), keeps them verbatim through preparation and publishes them via a macro-capable route.
Passes the snapshotToken from the prior page fetch on the update.
Verifies by content parity (tokens, ignoring whitespace and structural '>' markers), accepting cosmetic Markdown re-normalization.

Content parity ignores stable HTML-comment markers that Confluence drops outright on import (a platform limitation — the marker must remain in the prepared representation). Only markers escaped into visible text (`\<!--`, `<!--`) count as a parity failure.
